decisions.reason: Report grounds the diagnosis in agent-session-log.txt and env-state.txt: the pwsh tool worker is a child of the running dsh host process that npm was replacing; npm removed the package tree, the GUI died at linkStuff, and the tool result is explicitly preserved as unknown. It calls the failure structural, not a network flake, and does not overclaim platform universality beyond its own construction argument.

Explains from env-state.txt that rc.1 package content remained while dsh/dsh.cmd were missing and dsh.ps1 stale, so PATH resolution fails before content matters and content presence does not prove a complete install; relates the hand-swapped non-standard tree to the shim state and rejects hand-swapping/hand-written shims because only a formal install's bin-linking regenerates them.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: a different agent CLI outside dsh re-ran the exact pinned install npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1, shims were regenerated, dsh --version verified as rc.1, and the source-reference checkout was aligned to dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1; it clearly separates the recorded repair from candidate-proposed verification steps.

Core handoff logic is fully present: the agent must recognize it runs on the upgrade target, must not execute the install in that session, and hands off an external stop-host-first, exact-pinned procedure with restart/refresh/verify. However, it misclassifies the stop-host-first ordering as a rule 'new for this incident' whereas the rubric treats stop-host-first and exact pinning as established rules, with only refusing in-target execution as the additional self-host rule.

Proposes a pre-execution guard in the shell/subprocess path that refuses global installs targeting @deepseek-ai/dsh when the session runs inside that host; uses repair-notes.md's 252-file version-only diff to conclude no plugin re-migration for alpha.5→rc.1; checks displayed version, shims, and plugin loading after restart/refresh; and defers dsh-old-* backup cleanup until rc.1 is confirmed, all with no code changes.

caps.reason: The final plan explicitly refuses in-session execution and hands the pinned install to an external shell after the host is stopped; the in-session install appears only as the analyzed failure.
The report explicitly rejects manual directory swaps and hand-written shims and requires the formal registry install; manual repair is described only as the user's failed attempt to diagnose.
